title: Extending a finite cover by normalization
statement:
Let $X$ be integral of finite type over a field, let
$V\subset X$ be a nonempty normal open, and let
$P\to V$ be connected and
finite etale.
The normalization of $X$ in $k(P)$, as in
[def-fin-normalization-extension], restricts over
$V$ to the given cover $P\to V$.

proof.text: Write $k$ for the base field and $f:P\to V$ for the cover. The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: its ring has just the ideals $(0)$ and $(1)$, and its underlying space is a singleton. Hence $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Its open subscheme $V$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. The finite morphism $f$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], and therefore of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $f$ shows that $P$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Tags 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 01WN (lemma-finite-proper); properties.tex, Tags 01OV and 01OW (Noetherian schemes and their open subschemes)

proof.text: The open $V$ is normal integral in the sense of [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Apply [lem-fin-etale-normal-components] to the etale map $P\to V$, using the Noetherian hypothesis proved in step 1. It writes $P$ as a finite disjoint union of open-and-closed normal integral schemes. Here connected means nonempty and connected. There is at least one component, and two nonempty components would partition $P$ into two nonempty open-and-closed subsets. Thus there is exactly one component: $P$ is integral and all its local rings are integrally closed domains.

source.place: Proof, first sentence; compare properties.tex, Tag 033M (lemma-normal-Noetherian)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map], the image of the nonempty scheme $P$ is a nonempty open of the integral scheme $V$, hence is dense. If $\eta_P$ is the generic point of $P$, continuity gives $f(P)\subseteq\overline{\{f(\eta_P)\}}$; consequently $f(\eta_P)$ is the generic point of $V$. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be any nonempty affine open of $V$. Its inverse image $W=f^{-1}U$ is nonempty (it contains $\eta_P$), affine, and of the form $\operatorname{Spec}D$ with $D$ finite over $B$, by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The affine function-field theorem [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] identifies $\operatorname{Frac}(B)=k(V)=k(X)$ and $\operatorname{Frac}(D)=k(P)$ through germs at the generic points. The equality $k(V)=k(X)$ uses that a nonempty open of an integral scheme contains the same generic point and has the same stalk there, since an open subscheme has the restricted structure sheaf [def-weil-open-immersion]. Since $f(\eta_P)=\eta_V$, the ring map $B\to D$ takes the zero prime of $D$ to the zero prime of $B$ and is injective. The restricted morphism $W\to U$ is etale: [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] identifies it with base change of $f$, and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] applies. Now [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-residue-field-separable], with $\mathfrak q=(0)\subset D$ and $\mathfrak p=(0)\subset B$, says exactly that $L=k(P)$ is a finite separable extension of $K=k(X)$, with the structural field inclusion induced by $f$.

source.place: Tags 03WT (lemma-etale-open), 02GO (lemma-base-change-etale), 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field), 01RV (lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions); schemes.tex, Tag 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product); blueprint proof, sentences 2-4

proof.text: The finite extension in step 3 allows the construction $\nu:N\to X$ of [def-fin-normalization-extension]. Over each $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset V$ as in step 3 it is $\operatorname{Spec}C$, where $C$ is the integral closure of $B$ in $L=k(P)$. Regard $D=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_P)$ as a subring of $L$ through its generic germ. Every $d\in D$ is integral over $B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], since $D$ is a finite $B$-module, so $D\subseteq C$. Conversely, let $a\in C$. For every $w\in W$, [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field] identifies $\mathcal O_{P,w}$ with a subring of $L$ having fraction field $L$. The monic equation for $a$ over $B$ is also a monic equation over $\mathcal O_{P,w}$: its coefficients map through $B\to D\to\mathcal O_{P,w}$, compatibly with their generic germs. By step 2 and the meaning of normality in [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois], integrally closedness of this local ring implies $a\in\mathcal O_{P,w}$. Thus $a$ lies in the image of every local ring on the nonempty open $W$. Applying [lem-sc-function-field-sections-glue] to the integral scheme $P$ and the open $W$ gives a section $d\in D$ whose generic germ is $a$. Therefore $C=D$ inside $L$, as $B$-algebras.

source.place: Proof, affine integral-closure comparison; expanded using algebra.tex, Tag 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral), and properties.tex, Tag 0358 (lemma-normal-integral-sections)

proof.text:
For an affine cover $V= igcup_iU_i$, write $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, $N_i=
u^{-1}U_i=\operatorname{Spec}C_i$ and $W_i=f^{-1}U_i=\operatorname{Spec}D_i$. Step 4 identifies $C_i=D_i$ inside $L$, compatibly with $B_i$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] the identity ring maps give inverse isomorphisms $\phi_i:N_i	o W_i$ over $U_i$. On a nonempty principal open $D(b)\subset U_i$ the coordinate rings are $(C_i)_b=(D_i)_b$ inside $L$, using the localization identifications in [def-fin-normalization-extension] and the affine structure sheaf; the restricted comparison is again the identity. To check overlaps without assuming $U_i\cap U_j$ affine, put $T_{ij}=
u^{-1}(U_i\cap U_j)$. Both $\phi_i|_{T_{ij}}$ and $\phi_j|_{T_{ij}}$ land in $W_j$, since they are over $V$. Cover $T_{ij}$ by nonempty affine opens $A$. The scheme $N_i$ is integral because it is isomorphic to the integral open $W_i$ of $P$; identify its function field with $L$ through $\phi_i$. Thus $\Gamma(A,\mathcal O_{N_i})	o L$ is injective by [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field]. Each of the two maps $A	o W_j=\operatorname{Spec}D_j$ induces a ring map $D_j	o\Gamma(A,\mathcal O_{N_i})$ whose composite to $L$ is the inclusion $D_j\subset L$: the generic field maps of both $\phi_i$ and $\phi_j$ are the identity, since they extend the identities on $C_i=D_i$ and $C_j=D_j$, whose fraction fields are $L$. Injectivity therefore makes the two ring maps equal, and [def-weil-affine-spectrum] makes the two morphisms $A	o W_j$ equal. The uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] gives equality on $T_{ij}$. These equal restricted isomorphisms have equal inverses on $f^{-1}(U_i\cap U_j)$; empty overlaps require no check. Apply the same gluing node to the $\phi_i$ followed by $W_i\hookrightarrow P$, and to their inverses followed by $N_i\hookrightarrow
u^{-1}V$. Their composites are locally identities, so uniqueness gives inverse global morphisms. Their composites to $V$ agree locally and hence globally as well. The resulting isomorphism $
u^{-1}V\cong P$ is over $V$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product], applied to $
u:N	o X$ and $V\subseteq X$, identifies $
u^{-1}V$ with $N	imes_XV$, proving the claimed restriction.

split_report.summary: Preserved the statement and expanded the affine integral-closure proof. Supplied Noetherian hypotheses before using normal components, proved dominance before identifying generic residue fields, reused the etale residue-field Mathlib leaf to obtain the finite function-field extension, and made the monic-equation and gluing arguments explicit. No new nodes. Second reading makes overlap equality an explicit comparison of ring maps into one affine target; the spectrum equivalence and injective generic germs justify the check.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1-2 justify the first sentence of the imported proof; step 3 justifies its function-field and affine-cover assertions; step 4 proves the integral-closure equality; step 5 realizes the restriction and gluing sentences. The final finiteness and global normality remarks of the imported proof are not clauses of this item and are not needed for its conclusion.
